data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), which has raised €5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lonza, ticker LNZA), including companies such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy band—only 0 same-stage and 0 adjacent-stage peers met filtering thresholds. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression to the €5M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $12M.

This triangulation supports a valuation range of $11M (low) to $14M (high), with a median point of $12M. The narrow methodological basis—reflecting reliance on a single applicable approach rather than triangulated cross-checks—represents the primary analytical constraint. Key uncertainties center on the appropriateness of the 2.5x step-up multiplier to Hyperscale Power's specific profile and on the absence of direct peer comparables at seed stage within the sector, both of which merit investor diligence as additional financial data becomes available.
